metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct; apply a “cool-down” bias: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 5–10 day horizons post-spike.
- Sentiment history is uniformly neutral (0.00) across all examples — no sentiment-driven adjustment needed; model should not react to sentiment unless sentiment > 0.3 or < -0.3.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–30 day horizons: if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–20% for next 5–7 days; if below 1.5σ, increase by 5–10%.
- Model underestimates late-period (25–30 day) outcomes, especially in 2022 Q1; apply a “late horizon bias” correction: add 2–5% to forecast for days 25–30 if prior 10-day average > 75.00.
- No horizon-specific lag error observed — model does not systematically delay or accelerate price movement relative to true outcome.
